pr_title: Pass default values for `translate` through I18n
pr_body:
A default value can be a string that needs interpolation, Hash that needs resolution via the `:count` option, or a Proc that needs evaluation.  Therefore, pass default values through `I18n.translate` to handle these cases.

Fixes #26032.
Fixes #41277.
Fixes #41380.

issue_context.title: ActionView::Helpers::TranslationHelper.translate no longer executes Proc as default option in Rails 6.1
issue_context.body:
Rails 6.0.3.4:
```ruby
irb(main):001:0> I18n.t(:foobar, default: Proc.new { 'the default' })
=> "the default"
irb(main):002:0> include ActionView::Helpers::TranslationHelper
=> Object
irb(main):003:0> translate(:foobar, default: Proc.new { 'the default' })
=> "the default"
```

Rails 6.1.1:
```ruby
irb(main):001:0> I18n.t(:foobar, default: Proc.new { 'the default' })
=> "the default"
irb(main):002:0> include ActionView::Helpers::TranslationHelper
=> Object
irb(main):003:0> translate(:foobar, default: Proc.new { 'the default' })
=> #<Proc:0x000055d6898cc188@(irb):3>
```

review_comments:
Does ensuring that `alternatives` exists as an Array give us an opportunity to re-arrange this conditional?

```ruby
alternatives = Array.wrap(options.delete(:default) || []).compact

# ...
case alternatives.first
when Symbol
  key = alternatives.shift
when NilClass # maybe `when nil`?
  break false
else
  break I18n.translate(**options, default: alternatives)
end
```

Avoiding that array allocation was initially done in #32747, so I wanted to preserve that behavior.

Also, however, `translate(:missing, default: nil)` should return `nil`, while `translate(:missing, default: [])` should return a missing translation error.  To support these two cases, the `alternatives.present?` check differentiates between `[nil]` and `[]`.  Using `case alternatives.first` would only handle the former.

(And to make things more complicated, `translate(:missing, default: [nil])` should return a translation missing error, to mirror `I18n.translate`.  Hence the `compact` on line 74 and the `alternatives.first && ...` on line 98.)
